temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He invites Gary to a weekend retreat, but Gary declines because there is too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is dedicated but overworked, and that a brief retreat might help him rest and gain perspective.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Changed: Gary's refusal confirms that his overwork is severe and that he feels unable to step away even for a weekend.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is dangerously overcommitted to hospital work and that his health is at risk, but does not yet know the deeper reasons.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Continue trying to support Gary and encourage him to make time for rest, possibly by finding another way to help.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes that Gary is restless and avoids discussions about work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is overworked and hoped the retreat would help him relax, though he mainly attributes the problem to hospital obligations.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Changed: Gary's restlessness and avoidance suggest that his overwork is not just about professional duty; there may be deeper personal or work-related issues.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan suspects Gary is hiding something significant and that his overwork has more complicated causes than simple dedication.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Gently confront Gary and encourage him to open up about what is really going on.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After the confrontation, Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he is facing.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects there is more to Gary's overwork than professional obligations and wants to understand what is burdening him.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Changed: Gary's disclosure confirms that his overwork is driven by department-management pressure and personal challenges.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan understands the reasons behind Gary's behavior and believes Gary can find better balance with practical support.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Help Gary find a better balance by prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in with Gary. Gary reports progress, still faces challenges, and says he had time for a movie last weekend.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary can improve with support, but knows Gary still faces difficulties and may need continued encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Changed: Gary's reports and efforts show that he is making real progress toward a healthier work-life balance.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is actively improving and can maintain healthier habits with ongoing support.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Continue checking in, offering support, and encouraging Gary's progress.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance. Gary seems capable of managing on his own and thanks Ethan for his support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has been improving but may still benefit from regular check-ins and encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Changed: Gary's successful adjustment and ability to manage independently show that active intervention is no longer necessary.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary has achieved a healthy work-life balance and can maintain it on his own.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Step back from active support while letting Gary know he remains available if needed.
